title: What if a meteor shower never stopped?
premise: This week's Orionid meteor shower never ends. Instead, it keeps getting stronger every night.

intro.title: What if a *meteor shower* never stopped?
intro.subtitle: A HYPOTHETICAL SIMULATION

tooltip.label: REAL EVENT
tooltip.text: The Orionids peak every October. They're dust left behind by Halley's Comet.

beats.caption: It starts as a normal meteor shower. A few shooting stars an hour.

tooltip.label: FACT
tooltip.text: Most meteors are smaller than a grain of sand. They burn up about 100 km above you.

beats.caption: Each streak is a speck of dust hitting the air at tens of kilometers per second.
But the shower never ends. Every night, there are more.
Up in orbit, satellites start getting sandblasted.

banner.title: GPS AND SATELLITE TV DISRUPTED
banner.subtitle: Operators race to protect damaged satellites

beats.caption: Navigation, weather forecasts and satellite TV begin to glitch.
The night sky never goes dark anymore. It flickers until dawn.
Every so often, a bigger rock survives the fall and hits the ground.

tooltip.label: FACT
tooltip.text: Earth already sweeps up many tons of space dust every single day.

beats.caption: We already live inside a shower that never stops. It's just too small to see.
